transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-23 16:00 PST
Duration: 46 mins
Recording: Yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CTO, Blackbird AI), Elise Gomez (ML Eng), Samir Rao (Infra)

Summary:
Blackbird AI is evaluating options to move critical inference from OpenAI/Anthropic-hosted flows and a small on-prem vLLM/TGI cluster into a hybrid setup. Main concerns: latency spikes on tail, token cost unpredictability, and a need for private VPC deployment and KMS-managed keys for PII workloads. They want an eval showing parity on quality and an apples-to-apples perf/cost comparison.

Topics covered: migration constraints, model compatibility (vLLM/TGI), quantization options, caching/kv cache behavior, private deployment networking (VPC/peering), SOC2/KMS/SSO, rollout strategy and pricing.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:08] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here, CTO at Blackbird, we run some prod features on OpenAI right now and a small internal cluster for latency-sensitive routes.
[00:15] Elise Gomez: Elise, ML Eng. I'm focused on inference pipelines and our prompt quality metrics.
[00:20] Samir Rao: Samir, infra, I handle network/security and the internal vLLM nodes.
[00:24] Maya Chen: awesome, Omar and I are from Redwood, Omar will jump in on the technical bits. quick note, we'll take some notes, can we record?
[00:31] Rajiv Menon: yeah that's fine.

[00:45] Omar Patel: I want to start by understanding what 'lift' means for you. are you thinking full cutover from OpenAI, or a staged hybrid with dedicated capacity?
[00:56] Rajiv Menon: staged, probably. we'll keep OpenAI for low-volume fallback, but want our high-q, user-facing routes on a predictable stack. cost and tail latency are the drivers.
[01:06] Elise Gomez: also the quality parity — we use some RLHF-tuned variants and need to make sure outputs don't regress. we have eval suites.

[01:20] Omar Patel: good. two paths we typically see: Redwood Hosted (fast to start) or Dedicated pools for steady throughput; Private/VPC if you need customer-managed keys and no internet egress. you mentioned vLLM and TGI — are you running TGI today?
[01:36] Samir Rao: yes we have a small TGI front-end and vLLM on a couple of T4s for quick experiments, but it doesn't scale and KV cache management is messy.
[01:45] Maya Chen: when you say KV cache messy, can you expand?
[01:49] Samir Rao: sure, the cache gets invalidated on preemption and we lose prefix speedups; also memory fragmentation leads to jumpy latency.

[02:05] Rajiv Menon: and sometimes the TGI stack misreports token accounting vs OpenAI, so our cost models diverge.

[02:15] Omar Patel: that aligns with the common porting issues. we do automatic KV/prefix caching in the runtime, and our compiler picks kernels by seq len — tends to stabilize tail latency. you'll want to test with your prompt length distribution.

[02:33] Elise Gomez: how about quantization? we need to know if 8-bit/4-bit changes outputs. we ran int8 on a dev model and saw slight drift on negation cases.
[02:44] Omar Patel: good question, quantization is a trade — Redwood Optimize suggests model-specific profiles. for sensitive prompts you can pin to fp16 or mixed, for bulk inference use quantized variants. we can include eval-compare runs.

[03:01] Rajiv Menon: security questions — can we bring our own KMS? data residency? SSO?
[03:08] Maya Chen: yes. Private deployments support BYOK via KMS, we support customer HSM integrations in Dedicated/Private. SSO via SAML/Okta is standard. for Hosted we have encryption-at-rest and audit logs — but we can map specifics in the security pack.

[03:25] Samir Rao: network-wise, we need VPC peering and strict egress controls; some of our data can't leave subnet.
[03:31] Omar Patel: Private gives you a control-plane inside your VPC or a customer-managed control plane, otherwise Dedicated uses tenant isolation with VPC peering. We'll share the network diagrams.

[03:48] Elise Gomez: about eval parity — can you run our eval harness?
[03:52] Omar Patel: yes, we'll run your evals. ideally you give us the prompt sets, the reference outputs, and pass/fail thresholds. we do A/B vs your current provider and produce a quality drift report.

[04:06] Rajiv Menon: timeline: we want a pilot in two weeks — a 48-hour run with sample traffic to measure p99 and cost. is that doable?
[04:12] Omar Patel: doable, pending resources, we typically ask for representative prompt sets and traffic shape.

[04:25] Maya Chen: quick commercial note: many teams pick Dedicated for predictable budgets + Hosted as spillover; Private if compliance requires. We'll outline numbers and a burst policy.

[04:38] Rajiv Menon: price sensitivity is real — can you show per-token unit economics with and without quantization and cache hit rates?
[04:45] Omar Patel: yes, our Optimize tool projects per-token costs given batch size, cache hit, and quantization. we'll include scenarios: 1) current OpenAI run rate, 2) Dedicated with 30% cache hit, 3) Private fp16 with no quantization.

[05:05] Elise Gomez: on compatibility, our infra uses a custom serving shim on top of TGI — can Redwood consume the same model weights and config?
[05:14] Omar Patel: we support standard checkpoints (HF format), LoRA adapters, and common TGI variants. there are edge cases in custom kernels, but generally weights convert. we'll validate during the pilot.

[05:28] Rajiv Menon: we've had issues with tokenization differences vs OpenAI, e.g. whitespace handling that breaks some prompts.
[05:35] Omar Patel: tokenizers can vary; we normalize and include a tokenization parity step in the compatibility checklist.

[05:48] [06:00] Maya Chen: can you describe a minimal pilot scope you want from us?
[06:04] Omar Patel: for a 48-hour pilot: 1) provide 3 prompt suites (short, medium, long), 2) 50-100k tokens per day sample traffic or replay, 3) list of models to test (your OpenAI variants and your local TGI model), 4) eval scripts. we then run Hosted or Dedicated pilot with telemetry.

[06:26] Elise Gomez: we can do that, but we need assurances about data retention during pilot. we can't allow logs to be used for training.
[06:33] Maya Chen: agreed — Redwood has a training opt-out and we can sign a pilot data handling addendum. we'll put it in writing.

[06:45] Rajiv Menon: about rollout strategy — we want canary by user cohort then full cutover. if parity holds, we'll move 40% of traffic then 100% over 6 weeks.

[06:58] Omar Patel: that's standard. we also offer automatic fallback policies so if p99 latency exceeds threshold we reroute to OpenAI or a cheaper variant.

[07:12] Samir Rao: latency targets: for some routes we need <60ms tail; that's tough on GPU inference for long sequences.
[07:20] Omar Patel: agree — GPU options plus batching reduce cost but can increase latency; we sometimes keep microservices on CPU for extremely low-latency tiny prompts, or use cached KV paths. we can model your traffic to recommend compute type and batch windows.

[07:40] Elise Gomez: can you be specific about preemption — we run on spot instances for cost reasons, preemption kills cache. how do you handle that?
[07:48] Omar Patel: Redwood Dedicated supports reserved capacity to avoid preemption; if you do want spot we keep redundancy across nodes and persist KV layers so rewarm is bounded. we'll share RTO numbers.

[08:05] Rajiv Menon: any gotchas moving from Anthropic? we test there for safety filters.
[08:11] Omar Patel: safety models and filter behavior vary; Redwood can integrate a safety layer and reproduce the same heuristic checks, but we'll need to baseline with your safety prompts.

[08:25] [08:30] Maya Chen: any immediate blockers you foresee?
[08:33] Elise Gomez: we need to confirm SAML mapping for our Okta groups and RBAC before pilot, otherwise engineers won't have access.
[08:40] Samir Rao: and network firewall rules — we'll need a list of CIDRs and ports.

[08:47] Omar Patel: noted. we'll include a minimal SAML attribute map and a network allowlist in the security pack.

[09:00] Rajiv Menon: about model conversions — we have some LoRA adapters and custom tokenizers; how intrusive is the conversion?
[09:08] Omar Patel: mostly straightforward for HF/LoRA; custom tokenizers sometimes require a small shim layer. we can handle that in the pilot.

[09:18] Elise Gomez: what about reproducibility — we require determinism on certain prompts for audit features. are your runtimes deterministic?
[09:24] Omar Patel: single-threaded runs with fixed seeds are typically reproducible, but quantization and certain kernel fusions can introduce nondeterminism. we can pin configs for audit routes.

[09:40] Maya Chen: I'm going to share a checklist. Omar, do you want to call out the telemetry we collect?
[09:45] Omar Patel: we collect per-token latency, p50/p90/p99, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hits, and model output diffs vs reference. we also capture tokenization diffs.

[10:00] Rajiv Menon: output diffs — will you produce a human-readable drift report?
[10:04] Omar Patel: yes, automated with a hand-off summary for false positives/negatives flagged by your evals.

[10:15] Elise Gomez: one more question — are there constraints around regulatory logging for finance clients? we need WORM-style logs for some routes.
[10:22] Maya Chen: Redwood Console supports long-term retention and append-only export; for Private we can integrate your logging sink to satisfy WORM.

[10:33] Samir Rao: on costs — can Dedicated share GPUs across teams for cost efficiency? we have multiple product lines that could share capacity.

[10:38] Omar Patel: yes, multi-tenant pools with isolation and quotas are common. you can define route-level capacity and preempt policies.

[10:50] Rajiv Menon: OK let's talk about concrete deliverables. we need: security docs, pilot plan, cost model, and a shortlist of models to test.

[10:59] Maya Chen: action items covered. we'll send the security pack and a pilot intake template.

[11:08] [11:15] Elise Gomez: small nit — when you say 'model variants', do you support rolling back weights atomically? we've had issues with partial rollouts causing cache contamination.
[11:24] Omar Patel: yes, rollouts are atomic at the route level; cache keys are namespaced by model version to avoid contamination.

[11:35] Rajiv Menon: if performance looks good, what's a typical procurement cadence? we need legal for pilot terms and a later committed capacity agreement.
[11:42] Maya Chen: after pilot we provide a tailored contract: pilot terms → engineering SLA → reserved capacity proposal; procurement usually takes 2–4 weeks depending on legal.

[11:55] Samir Rao: any references or case studies for a similar financial/PII-sensitive migration?

[12:01] Maya Chen: yes, we can share an anonymized case study where we ran a Dedicated pilot and moved critical routes off public provider for a regulated client. I'll attach a one-pager.

[12:10] Elise Gomez: perfect.

[12:15] Omar Patel: quick technical note — about your token weirdness with OpenAI, we recommend running tokenizer parity first. difference in byte pair splits explains many of the mismatches.

[12:27] Rajiv Menon: makes sense. anything else?

[12:30] Maya Chen: recap of next steps: Maya to send security pack by Friday (11/26), Omar to run compatibility checklist and prep pilot topology, Blackbird to send prompts and infra diagram by Thursday (11/25). We'll plan a 48-hour throughput pilot week of 11/29 and follow-up for deep network dive week of 12/6.

[12:57] Elise Gomez: sounds good. thanks for the flexibility.
[13:00] Rajiv Menon: thanks all.

End of transcript

Notes on transcription: occasional word substitutions (TGI sometimes transcribed as 'tee gee eye' vs 'T.G.I'), speaker turns occasionally collapsed, timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: Pilot intake template (link), security pack (to be shared), anonymized case study one-pager, benchmark sheet (link).
